coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Marriage
That Feels Distant
coverDek: For the silence that crept in, the argument that never finished, and the vow that's still holding even when it doesn't feel like it — five prayers for the marriage nobody sees the hard parts of.

points.hook: Lord, we used to talk about everything. Now we're just... careful.
paragraphs: We used to stay up talking about nothing in particular, and somewhere along the way the conversations got shorter and more careful. Neither of us meant for this to happen — it just got quiet, one ordinary week at a time. Lord, teach us to talk again before the silence becomes a habit neither of us knows how to break.
points.verseText: A threefold cord is not quickly broken.

points.hook: I decree over this marriage: what tries to divide us will not stand.
paragraphs: I decree over this marriage: every spirit assigned to divide what God has joined will not stand, in the name of Jesus! We agree together, right now, against every scheme aimed at our home — not offense against offense, but one mind, one house. What God has joined, no silence, no pride, and no outside voice will separate!
points.verseText: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

points.hook: Notice what the last unfinished argument is still doing to your body.
paragraphs: Notice what you're carrying in your shoulders after the last argument that didn't get finished. Unresolved anger doesn't just sit in the conversation — it sits in your chest, your sleep, the way you flinch before your spouse even speaks. Lord, don't let the sun go down on what we haven't said; loosen what we're both still holding before tonight is over.
points.verseText: Let not the sun go down upon your wrath.

points.hook: Somebody's marriage is quietly struggling because both of you stopped asking for help.
paragraphs: Somebody in this family is quietly struggling in their marriage because both of them got too proud or too tired to say it out loud. Family, a marriage was never meant to be held together alone — two are better than one, because if either one falls, there's someone there to lift them back up. If that's you tonight, let someone carry this with you.
points.verseText: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

points.hook: Child, I was in the room the day you two became one.
paragraphs: Child, I was in the room the day you two became one, and I haven't left since — not during the good years, and not during this hard one. What I joined together, I am still holding together, even on the nights it doesn't feel like it. Rest in that tonight. I'm not finished with either of you.
points.verseText: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named what your marriage is carrying, don't carry it in silence — come back tomorrow for the next series.
